entry.max_stay: 30 days, extendable through the Bureau of Immigration
entry.pre_arrival: eTravel registration and electronic health declaration for a QR code. Onward or return ticket within 30 days.
entry.other: Declare cash over PHP50,000 or over US$10,000 in foreign currency. Children under 15 not with a parent may need a Waiver of Exclusion Ground.

tourism.detail: Australian passport holders are on the published visa-free list for tourism or business.
tourism.next: Complete eTravel in the 72-hour window and carry onward travel.

meetings.detail: Official guidance names meetings, contract negotiations and international conference attendance.
meetings.next: Keep the visit in the meeting and negotiation lane unless a petitioner activates work permission.

conference.detail: International conference attendance fits temporary business.
conference.next: If the organiser adds a talk, workshop or fee, ask them to switch to the speaker route.

unpaid-speaking.route: BI classification required for a sub-three-month appearance; Commercial SWP is a candidate, not a confirmed fit
unpaid-speaking.detail: The older official checklist includes lecturers, researchers and trainers with or without compensation, while the current service page states three-to-six-month gainful employment.
unpaid-speaking.next: Have the Philippine organiser give BI the exact days, duties and compensation and obtain the route in writing.

paid-speaking.detail: Paid short-term work needs a Special Work Permit; speakers aren't named on the pages read.
paid-speaking.next: Ask the Bureau of Immigration through the host.

book-launch.route: BI classification for the active appearance; Philippine publisher or bookseller for sales
book-launch.detail: The lecturer and trainer checklist suggests a possible SWP lane, but a short reading or launch still needs BI confirmation because of the current three-month minimum wording.
book-launch.next: Separate the appearance, rights meetings, royalties and physical sales, then have the host ask BI for the exact route.

ai-teaching.route: BI classification for short training; AEP plus 9(g) for longer employment
ai-teaching.detail: The older SWP checklist covers lecturers and trainers; current Commercial SWP duration starts at three months. Longer Philippine employment uses the labour-permit and pre-arranged employment system.
ai-teaching.next: Ask the host to classify the dates first, then choose SWP or the AEP and 9(g) sequence.

remote-work.route: Digital Nomad Visa authorised; operational applications and Australian reciprocity both need confirmation
remote-work.detail: Executive Order 86 authorises a one-year renewable DNV and ties nationality eligibility to reciprocal treatment, but current operational application availability for Australians was not established.
remote-work.next: Ask the Philippine mission to confirm both a live application channel and Australian eligibility.

entrepreneur.route: SIRV or SVEG depending capital and employment generation
entrepreneur.detail: Investor residence starts at US$75,000 under SIRV; SVEG requires at least ten full-time Filipino workers. A separate startup-visa route was not confirmed as operational.
entrepreneur.next: Choose capital investment or employment generation before modelling the entity and operating role.

trade.route: Visa-free negotiations first; SEC/DTI and work permissions for local operation
trade.detail: Trade meetings and contract negotiation are easy; a local branch, selling operation or management role adds commercial and work layers.
trade.next: Keep the first trip to partners, markets and setup choices, then map the entity and operating role.

artist.route: Special Work Permit, filed by the Philippine promoter or organiser
artist.detail: Artists and performers who perform before an audience for a fee need a Special Work Permit (initially 3 months, extendable by 3).
artist.next: Ask the organiser to file the Special Work Permit with the Bureau of Immigration.

mixed-mission.route: One Philippine lead host plus written BI classification of the complete schedule
mixed-mission.detail: The candidate SWP categories are useful, but current duration wording prevents assuming that a day or week professional tour fits.
mixed-mission.next: Choose one organiser to submit all venues, dates, payments and duties to BI.

filming.route: Film Location Engagement Desk (FDCP) plus local government shooting location permits
filming.detail: The Film Development Council's desk helps foreign productions with permits and crew entry; location permits come from local governments under the 2026 DILG and FDCP guidelines. Apply at least two months before production; a local partner is advised.
filming.next: Contact the Film Location Engagement Desk.

research.route: Ask the Embassy of the Philippines, Yarralumla
research.detail: No official statement on this activity was read. Easy entry isn't permission to work.
research.next: Ask the Embassy of the Philippines, Yarralumla which visa covers it, in writing.

volunteering.route: Ask the Embassy of the Philippines, Yarralumla
volunteering.detail: No official statement on this activity was read. Easy entry isn't permission to work.
volunteering.next: Ask the Embassy of the Philippines, Yarralumla which visa covers it, in writing.

laws.rule: Penalties for drug offences are severe. They include long jail terms, including life imprisonment, for even small amounts. A major clampdown on drugs - the war on drugs - has been underway since 2016. There are mandatory jail sentences for possessing even small amounts of illicit drugs. Thousands have been arrested and a large number of people have been killed in drug-related violence.
laws.heading: Drugs

laws.rule: The Philippines also has strong laws against child sex crimes and human trafficking. Authorities have arrested and prosecuted a number of foreigners, including Australians, for these offences. Sentences can include life imprisonment. It's illegal to take photos of official buildings for publication. It's illegal to take part in political rallies if you're not a Filipino citizen. Authorities may deport you or cancel your visa for being involved.
laws.heading: Other laws

laws.rule: You can use a current Australian driver's licence (digital driver's licences may not be accepted) for up to 90 days after you arrive. After that, you need to get a Philippines licence.

money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: The local currency is the Philippine peso (PHP). You can easily convert AUD for PHP at airports, banks, shopping centres, tourist locations, in major cities and towns. ATMs are widely available. International credit cards are generally accepted in hotels, restaurants and higher-end shops, particularly in cities and larger towns. However, it's advisable to keep some cash. Card skimming occurs.
